samples.summary: Read-only enforcement is an EditorAPI method allowlist, but `getDoc()`/`getStore()` hand out unrestricted CRDT write handles, so the boundary has to be re-implemented in every out-of-module consumer
samples.evidence: The only read-only enforcement for docs is the `MUTATING_METHODS` no-op loop at `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4023-4041`. `getDoc()` and `getStore()` are deliberately NOT in that list, and both return live write-capable handles (`Doc.deleteText` / `Doc.insertText`, `YorkieDocStore`). `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:65-68` takes exactly those handles and drives `FindReplaceState.replaceMatch` → `doc.deleteText`/`doc.insertText` (`packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:78-87`), which is precisely why a viewer on an anonymous share link could rewrite document text before this delta (`readOnly` there comes from `resolved.role === "viewer"`, `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:278`, and the server-side Yorkie auth webhook is shadow-mode-by-default per `packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-105`, so the client flag is the effective boundary). This delta fixes the one known consumer by duplicating the check in the component (`docs-find-bar.tsx:134,143,288`) rather than at the boundary that hands out the handle. Attacker path for the next occurrence: any future component that calls `editor.getDoc()` and forgets a `readOnly` prop reopens the same viewer-write hole with no compile-time or lint signal. No currently-reachable exploit remains (I checked the other `getDoc()`/`getStore()` callers — `docs-comments-controller.ts:146,238,358` read `.document` only and gate composition at line 235; `docs-export-button.tsx:47` reads; `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:351` reads a font registry and is not rendered for viewers, `shared-document.tsx:305`), hence hardening severity rather than an active exploit.

samples.summary: The only write gate protecting a viewer from CRDT writes in this component is an optional prop that fails open when omitted
samples.evidence: `readOnly?: boolean` with `readOnly = false` (docs-find-bar.tsx:34,47) means a caller that mounts `DocsFindBar` without the prop gets the fully writable replace path back — `handleReplace`/`handleReplaceAll` (lines 132-148) reach `doc.deleteText`/`doc.insertText` directly, outside the editor's `MUTATING_METHODS` neutralization. Today the sole call site passes it (`docs-view.tsx:618`), so this is not exploitable now; but for a component whose entire authorization story is this one flag, defaulting to permissive means a forgotten prop is a silent viewer-write regression rather than a type error. A required `readOnly: boolean` prop would make omission a compile error — noting that `packages/frontend` has no `tsc` lane, so even that only helps at author time.

finding.summary: Find-bar replace path has no read-only gate and bypasses the EditorAPI read-only neutralization entirely
finding.evidence: `DocsFindBar` takes no `readOnly` prop and `handleReplace`/`handleReplaceAll` (docs-find-bar.tsx:121,130 — both touched by this diff) call `state.replaceActive()` / `state.replaceAll()` on a `FindReplaceState` built from `editor.getDoc()` and `editor.getStore().snapshot()` (lines 54-57). That writes the CRDT directly, skipping every guard the codebase relies on for viewers: the `MUTATING_METHODS` no-op allowlist at `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4018-4036` and all `TextEditor` `readOnly` guards. The diff wires `editor?.clearImageSelection()` into exactly these two handlers and the accompanying design text (`docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md`) blesses the seam as "runs straight against the `Doc` the find bar holds ... bypassing the editor's own mutation entry points" — but no permission check was added alongside it. Attacker path: a `viewer`-role share link (`shared-document.tsx:278` `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`) renders `DocsView` read-only; the find bar is opened with Cmd/Ctrl+F (deliberately allowed in read-only, `text-editor.ts:903`) and, if `showReplace` is ever true, the Replace / All buttons write to the shared document. Today the only thing preventing that is that `showReplace` is set solely by `onFindReplaceRequest`, whose Cmd/Ctrl+H keydown falls after the `readOnly` early-return at `text-editor.ts:894-912`, so I could not complete the exploit through the shipped UI — the boundary is one unrelated keydown branch in another package, with no gate at the mutation itself. This matters more than usual here because the branch's own docs state the server-side Yorkie auth webhook defaults to shadow mode (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset ⇒ allow, `packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:87`), making the client `readOnly` flag the effective write boundary for anonymous share links. Suggested fix: pass `readOnly` into `DocsFindBar` and early-return in both handlers (and hide the replace row), mirroring `showCut`/`showPaste` gating

verdict.reason: The claimed absence is false in this repository. `DocsFindBar` declares a `readOnly?: boolean` prop (docs-find-bar.tsx:34, destructured at :47) whose doc-comment explicitly cites the `MUTATING_METHODS` bypass as the reason the gate lives in the component. Both mutation handlers early-return on it before touching the CRDT: `handleReplace` at :134 (`if (readOnly || !state || state.activeIndex < 0) return;`) guarding `state.replaceActive()` at :136, and `handleReplaceAll` at :143 guarding `state.replaceAll()` at :145. The Enter-key entry point (`handleReplaceKeyDown` :178) funnels into `handleReplace`, so it is covered. The replace row is additionally not rendered for viewers: `{showReplace && !readOnly && ...}` at :288. The gate is wired at the call site, not left to the `false` default: docs-view.tsx:613-619 renders `<DocsFindBar ... readOnly={readOnly} />` at line 618, from the same `readOnly` prop (docs-view.tsx:105,139) that drives `initialize(...)` at :327 and the other viewer-gated overlays, so the viewer-role share-link path reaches the bar with `readOnly === true`. A dedicated regression test pins this behavior (docs-find-bar-read-only.test.tsx:61-107): a viewer can search but `doc.deleteText`/`doc.insertText` are never called and the replace row/buttons are absent. This is exactly the fix the finding suggests, already present. The finding itself conceded no exploit could be completed; the real reason is that the mutation is gated, not just the Cmd/Ctrl+H keydown branch.

finding.summary: Server-side write authorization for viewer share links is shadow-mode by default, so the client `readOnly` flag this change widens is the only effective write boundary
finding.evidence: `YorkieAuthController` computes the per-document read/write decision but returns ALLOW whenever `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE !== 'true'` (constructor at :86-88, shadow branch at :97-105); packages/backend/README.md:111 documents `false` as the default. `readOnly` in the frontend is derived purely client-side (`packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:152`, `readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'`) and passed into `initialize()`. In a default deployment, therefore, any client-side read-only gap in the docs editor is a real write for an anonymous viewer, not a UX inconsistency. This is pre-existing and outside the diff, but it is the assumption the change under review leans on: the diff deliberately opens `handleImageMouseDown`, the textarea focus and the key/clipboard handlers to viewers and compensates entirely with client-side `readOnly` checks (the design doc it adds says so explicitly at docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:292). Reported so the widened surface is weighed against the enforcement posture rather than assumed to be backstopped by the server.

verdict.reason: All claimed evidence verified in-repo. yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-88 sets enforce only when YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'; :97-105 discards every deny decision and returns ALLOW in the default (shadow) configuration, nullifying the viewer/editor role check at :200 (`needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`). packages/backend/README.md:111 confirms `false` is the documented default. No compensating server gate exists: auth.controller.ts:76-84 mints a Yorkie token for any share token without inspecting role, explicitly deferring role validation to the webhook. The frontend boundary is purely client-side (shared-document.tsx:278 `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`, forwarded at :306-311), and the repo's own design doc states this at docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:299-302. Concrete vector: an anonymous viewer-link holder calls POST /auth/yorkie-token/share, attaches with verb 'rw', and the webhook logs '[shadow] would deny' while allowing the write. Cannot refute as not-present (code matches), already-guarded (only role check is the one being discarded), or out-of-scope (weakened authorization gate on the enforced write path is squarely in the Security lane; pre-existing/out-of-diff does not exempt it under the rubric).
